name_reason: Complies with fd2_<domain>_<descriptor>. The '22_27_28' are meaningful chapter IDs (FD2 chapters 01-30 are real domain IDs), not Ghidra address residue (no relation to 0x20A87). '_shared' is accurate: the same code is dispatched for all three chapters via data_fd2_chapter_post_action_handler_table[21]/[26]/[27] (verified: all three entries hold 0x20A87). 'post_action' matches the turn-cycle post-action handler role. No address-suffix residue.
purpose: Shared per-chapter turn-cycle post-action handler for chapters 22, 27, 28: runs the default win/lose check and adds a lose override when the must-protect ally at runtime_char slot 1 is dead.
logic_summary: Calls fd2_check_battle_end_condition() (default: win if no enemies alive, lose if protagonist runtime_char[0] dead, else continue). Then calls fd2_check_char_is_dead(1); if it returns non-zero (runtime_char[1].flags bit0 set), writes data_fd2_chapter_event_or_battle_end_code (0x53ECC) = 1 (game over). The PUSH 0x8 / CALL __CHK at entry is the Watcom stack-probe prologue (8 = local frame/probe size), an artifact, not a real argument. Dispatched (0 direct callers); reached only via the per-chapter handler table at 0x51B19 indices 21/26/27 (chapters 22/27/28).

params.name: event_arg
params.semantics: Dispatch-contract argument (the active char_idx some sibling handlers receive) / Watcom __CHK-prologue artifact. Unused by this body. Name is consistent with all sibling post-action handlers in chpost.c and describes the dispatch contract; no address residue.
params.reason: Accurately reflects the unused dispatch/__CHK-prologue argument; matches the file-wide naming convention for these dispatched handlers; no address suffix.

returns.semantics: No return value. Effect is conveyed via the global data_fd2_chapter_event_or_battle_end_code (0x53ECC): set to 1 on lose (ally at slot 1 dead); otherwise left as written by fd2_check_battle_end_condition (0 continue / 1 protagonist dead / 2 victory).

comment_original_issue: Both the src comment and the Ghidra plate claimed 'char[1] is the same protected NPC across all three chapters (a continuous protect-ally story arc)'. This is factually wrong: the walkthrough lose conditions show the slot-1 ally is 希爾法 (Sylpha) in chapter 22 but 悠妮 (Yuni) in chapters 27 and 28 (chapter 22 失敗條件: 索爾死亡/希爾法死亡; chapter 27/28 失敗條件: 索爾死亡/悠妮死亡). The shared handler is justified by identical lose-condition STRUCTURE (default check + one extra protected ally at slot 1), not by a single shared character identity. The comment also did not note that the default check already handles the protagonist (slot 0) death.
notes: Verified via dispatch table read at 0x51B19: little-endian entries -> index 21 (off 0x54 @ 0x51B6D), 26 (off 0x68 @ 0x51B81), 27 (off 0x6C @ 0x51B85) all = 0x20A87, matching the three DATA xrefs and chapters 22/27/28 (chapter = index+1). Disassembly confirms PUSH 0x8/CALL __CHK prologue, CALL fd2_check_battle_end_condition, PUSH 0x1/CALL fd2_check_char_is_dead/ADD ESP,4, TEST EAX,EAX/JZ, MOV dword [0x53ECC],1. fd2_check_battle_end_condition decompile confirms protagonist (slot 0) death is the default lose path, so slot-1 check is the added must-protect ally. Walkthrough cross-check (fd2-knowledge chapters 22/27/28) is the source of the corrected story rationale. Code logic is correct; only the explanatory comment rationale was wrong -> not a logic issue.
